# Cosmu

> Autonomous crypto-trading platform on Binance spot. A scheduled pipeline of agents (Research → Trader → deterministic Validator → Execution) runs trading "bots" against a venue; future index- and research-agents read/write a shared signals store. The model's *decision* and the venue's *execution* are always kept as separate records.

This file maps the app for LLM agents. The web app (Next.js) is a thin UI over an Express API; its `/app/api/*` routes proxy to the API with a server-side secret key. Contracts live in `@cosmu/shared` (Zod schemas).

## Architecture (in the repo, not served over HTTP)
- ARCHITECTURE.md: Non-obvious implementation facts the code relies on (pipeline shape, double-fire protection, USDT/USDC agnosticism, xAI provider quirks, MCP tools). Read this first.
- AGENTS.md: Coding-agent entrypoint and conventions.

## Core concepts
- Bot: a scheduled agent that runs one Research→Trader→Validator→Execution cycle against an explicit venue. All agents live in one list, differentiated by `venue` and whether execution is enabled.
- Run: one execution of the pipeline. Produces agent_steps (product timeline) and run_llm_calls (provider telemetry).
- Decision vs Execution: never collapsed. Prompt version, model profile, raw model output, parsed decision, validation result, order intent, venue execution result, and portfolio state are distinct records.
- Source → Record → Signal → Index: the data model for ingesting external data, standardizing it into signals, and deriving index views. Tables exist; ingestion/runners are being wired.

## Web sections (pages)
- /: Dashboard — agents overview, performance, venue health, spend estimates.
- /bots, /bots/[botId]: Agent list and per-agent run history, prompts, live positions.
- /research: Research experiments, datasets, evaluations.
- /signals: Standardized signals capture and triage.
- /sentiment: Market pulse signals.
- /prompts, /prompt-lab: Prompt library with versioning, and prompt experiments.
- /spending: LLM token ledger and cost estimates.
- /settings: Model, venue, trader-prompt config and feature toggles.

## API surface (Express; called via the web proxy with x-api-key)
- GET /health: Liveness.
- GET /dashboard: Cached dashboard payload (prices, balances, agents, spend).
- GET /mcp/tools: Registered agent-facing tool definitions.
- Bots: GET/POST /bots, GET/PATCH /bots/:botId, POST /bots/:botId/run, POST /bots/:botId/kill, GET /bots/:botId/runs, GET /bots/:botId/positions.
- Runs: GET /runs/:runId, GET /runs/:runId/llm-calls.
- Research: /research/* (sessions, specs, datasets, evaluations, candidates, memory, data-sources).
- Signals & Indexes: /signals/*, /indexes/*.
- Sources & Tradability: /sources/*, /tradability/*.
- Prompts: /prompts/*, /trader-prompts/*.
- Settings & Models & Venues: /settings/*, /models, /venues/*.
- Ops (internal): GET /internal/diagnostics, GET /internal/background-jobs, POST /internal/scheduler/tick, POST /internal/background-jobs/:jobId/run, GET /spend/llm.

## Notes for agents
- Runtime automation (scheduler, guardian, market-data cache, catalog syncs) runs on Railway, not Vercel.
- Never bypass the deterministic validator (services/validator.ts) or the global kill switch.
- Tools are registered in apps/api/src/mcp/index.ts; agent-facing ones are auto-exposed to the trader.
